prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the vertical brick wall immediately to the right of the camera wearer (within 0.3 to 1.5 metres, brightest on the right edge) and the receding floor of the construction room about 2.5 to 3.5 metres below. In frame 1, the head and shoulders of a second worker standing on the scaffold platform about 0.8 to 1.2 metres directly below the camera wearer appear as a bright foreground blob at the bottom center, while the worker in blue on the ground floor (~3 metres below and to the left) is barely distinguishable as a faint dark-grey silhouette next to circular pans and a sand pile. Across frames 4 and 5, as the ground worker lifts a round mortar pan up toward the scaffold and the camera wearer reaches out with their left hand (within 0.4 to 0.7 metres in frame 5), both the raised pan (~1 to 1.5 metres away) and the reaching forearm stand out clearly as bright foreground shapes against the dark floor, clarifying their vertical proximity better than the cluttered RGB image. However, the depth map is unreliable for the ground-level objects, bricks, sacks, and the lower worker in frames 1 to 3, where low contrast merges them into a nearly uniform black background.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map fails to detect any of the people, walls, scaffolds, or construction materials, leaving frames 1 and 3 completely blank and detecting only a few isolated shapes in frames 2, 4, and 5. Using the RGB strip for context, the scene actually contains a worker on the ground (~3 metres below) scooping mortar into round metal pans in frames 1 to 3 (with pans and a shovel within their arm's reach, ~0.5 metres away), another worker just below the camera wearer (~1 metre away) in frame 1, and piles of bricks and sacks 2.5 to 4 metres away on the floor. The segmentation map only captures the round mortar pans—mislabelled as a 'cup' in frame 2 (~3 metres below) and 'bowl' in frames 4 and 5 (at ~3 metres on the floor and ~1 to 1.5 metres when lifted toward the camera wearer)—and highlights the crisp circular boundary of the raised pan in frames 4 and 5. It is highly unreliable overall, misclassifying bricks on the floor as 'carrot' in frame 4, labelling the camera wearer's outstretched left arm (0.5 metres away at bottom left) as a 'spoon' in frame 5, and covering almost the entire frame 5 background with a false 'dining table' mask.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely black across all 5 frames, failing to detect any body or hand skeletons despite multiple people and limbs being visible in the RGB strip. In the RGB scene, a worker in a hat and red shirt is positioned directly below the camera wearer (~0.8 to 1.2 metres away, partially occluded by the bottom frame edge) in frame 1 facing toward the ground floor, and another worker in light blue is on the floor (~3 metres below and to the left) bending over a mortar pan in frames 1 to 3 before turning their face upward to look directly at the camera wearer in frame 4 while lifting the pan overhead. In frame 5, the ground worker is largely occluded beneath the raised pan (~1 to 1.2 metres below the camera wearer), while the camera wearer's own bare left arm and hand enter the lower-left foreground (within 0.5 metres, within arm's reach of the raised pan) alongside their foot on the scaffold ladder at the bottom center. Because the pose estimator is completely unreliable under this steep top-down egocentric viewpoint and heavy self-occlusion, it provides no spatial information beyond what must be read from the RGB frames.
